talks.title: Ransomware Rap
talks.teaser: Evaluates ransomware Rap and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
Ransomware Warning Song

This DragonJAR presentation is a musical performance about ransomware rather than a technical talk. Lyrics describe malware arriving via phishing email, silently encrypting disks, and displaying ransom demands paid in Bitcoin without guarantees.

Attack Narrative

The song portrays classic ransomware stages: disguised traps, neglected links, hijacked data, black screens declaring no backups, and attackers holding victims "under fire" without warning or mercy.

Defensive Guidance

Repeated choruses urge maintaining backups, updated antivirus, firewalls, two-factor authentication, password hygiene, and security awareness. The performance frames human error—opening the wrong link—as the common entry point.

Conference Format

Delivered as a rap with music and applause, the piece uses entertainment to reinforce basic cyber hygiene rather than presenting new research or technical analysis.

talks.summary: Overview: Physical security is an oft-overlooked but critical prerequisite for good information security. Software has leaked into every aspect of modern life and now controls access to physical resources as well as to business and personal information. When critically examined, physical security policies and mechanisms have (perhaps have *always*) contained substantial snake oil components, including back doors, extensive use of protection by "security through obscurity", and piece solutions which ignore their environmental context or need to function in a system.
